What if you stayed underwater too long?
Most people last thirty to ninety seconds.
First, cold water hits your face.
Blood rushes from your arms to your core.
Your spleen squeezes out extra red cells.
But carbon dioxide keeps building up.
That's the burning urge to breathe!
Your chest starts to twitch and jerk.
Your brain needs it the most.
Push too far and you black out.
Even when you feel totally fine.
That's why you never swim alone!
A Weddell seal? Over an hour!
So... how long can you last on dry land?
